correctness.rationale: One-variable antiderivative tests give each conditional law. Since a conditional expectation of sine lies in [-1,1], the coordinate bounds hold almost surely and therefore on support. Orthogonal projection gives E[dot x^2]=Var(sin y)-b^2 Var(x), cyclically, and summing gives the activity budget. If the first defect is zero, continuity makes dot x vanish on support; along every support orbit x is constant and sin y is constant. A continuous real trajectory confined to a discrete sine level set has y constant; the same argument makes z constant and the orbit an equilibrium. Cyclic symmetry gives the other two equality cases. The exact verifier correctly checks the residual-square algebra and summed budget.

value.rationale: The Thomas flow is a standard cyclic-feedback chaotic model. A universal stationary calibration of every nonlinear drive, a sharp support box, and three individually rigid variance-speed diagnostics give reusable exact tests for recurrent states and simulations. The content is broader than a single routine average and its equality mechanism uses the special cyclic sine architecture.

final_claim: For the Thomas cyclic sine flow with 0<b<1, every compact invariant measure satisfies the three cyclic conditional laws E[sin y|x]=bx and their rotations, is supported in [-1/b,1/b]^3, and has exact coordinate variance-speed defects; any one zero defect forces equilibrium support, so all three inequalities are strict for every nonequilibrium stationary state.
